title: Proper projection factor of a compactification on bounded constructible complexes
statement: Let $\ell$ be prime, $k$ a field of positive characteristic different from $\ell$, and $f:X\to Y$ a morphism of separated finite-type $k$-schemes with a compactification $X\xrightarrow{i}Z\xrightarrow{g}Y$, $i$ open and $g$ proper [def-nagata-compactification, sk-def-sfb-dc-setting, def-weil-proper-morphism]. Let $\Lambda$ be a commutative condensed ring [sk-def-sfb-condensed-ring] in the class IsEllAdicFinitenessCoefficient: the continuous condensed finite extension $E$ of $\mathbf Q_\ell$, its valuation ring (either supported integral presentation), or $\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$. Put $\Lambda_T=p_T^*\Lambda$ [sk-def-sfb-pulled-back-coefficients]. For bounded constructible complexes $K$ on $X$ and $B$ on $Y$, put $A=Di_!K$, bounded constructible by extension by zero [sk-def-sfb-bounded-constructible, def-sfb-dc-open-lower-shriek]. With the relative derived tensor [sk-def-sfb-derived-tensor-hom], the actual projection component $Rg_*A\otimes^{\mathbf L}B\to Rg_*(A\otimes^{\mathbf L}Lg^*B)$ is invertible. Here it is precisely the adjoint under $Lg^*\dashv Rg_*$ [sk-def-sfb-module-derived-pushpull] of the actual oplax pullback tensor comparison followed by $\varepsilon_A\otimes 1$, not an unspecified map between these endpoints.

proof.text: For an isomorphism a of commutative condensed rings, scalar extension is an exact equivalence. The scalar unit and counit are invertible, so derivedPushHom a f is invertible by its mate formula. In coefficientProjectionSquare every companion arrow is invertible. If projection is invertible after scalar extension, cancel these companions and reflect invertibility through the scalar equivalence. The transported complex remains bounded constructible by the coefficient-realization comparison.

proof.text: For a finite normed extension E, choose its algebraic embedding into PadicAlgCl and its finite field range F. The existing embedding_isometry calculation identifies the norms. Postcomposition with this field isomorphism identifies the continuous condensed rings, and its restriction identifies any specified closed unit ball with the embedded integers of F. For an original embedded integral coefficient, use its induced norm and the same unit-ball argument. These are isomorphisms of ring objects, including their specified multiplication.

proof.text: Identify the embedded integer coefficient of F with DerivedNakayama.integerRing on ULift F by integerRingSheafIso. Transport the integralLfpConstantModelComparison along the WithAbs-to-embedded-to-spectral coefficient isomorphisms using comparison_transport. Degreewise this equates general bounded constructibility with the finite-constant-model predicate required by integralProperDirectImageAndFormulas. Its final conjunct proves projection invertible for the two transported complexes; reflect back through the coefficient isomorphisms.

proof.text: For continuous field coefficients apply isIso_properProjectionMap_boundedConstructible_rational over the finite field F and reflect back. For the condensed algebraic closure apply that theorem directly. Eliminate the four constructors of IsEllAdicFinitenessCoefficient, covering continuous fields, embedded integral coefficients, algebraic closure, and closed unit balls. The input complexes are exactly the open extension of K and B.
